title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 196
paragraphs: The Carthaginians also say this: there is a place in Libya, and people living there, outside the Pillars of Heracles. When they come to them, they unload their merchandise from their ships, lay it out in order along the beach, and then go back aboard their ships and send up a smoke signal. The natives, seeing the smoke, come down to the sea and lay down gold as payment for the merchandise and then withdraw to a distance from the goods. The Carthaginians then come ashore and examine it; and if the gold seems to them a fair price for their merchandise, they take it up and go their way. But if not, they go back aboard their ships and wait; and the others come up and add more gold to what is already there, until the Carthaginians are satisfied. They say that neither side wrongs the other; for the Carthaginians do not touch the gold until it matches the value of their merchandise, nor do the natives touch the merchandise until the Carthaginians have taken the gold.
